races.name: Sky Bet Proud To Support Young Lives Vs Cancer Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needed his reappearance run and drops to attractive mark from peak form last summer
runners_data.comment: On a reduced mark but went off the boil at end of last season, and well beaten on return
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up five times last May-August and he's on an attractive mark on that form; he may have needed last week's reappearance run at Ripon but was well beaten, which was also the case on his final few outings last season.

runners_data.name: Madame De Sevigne
runners_data.note: Patient ride required, strong closer who has shown her best form when held up for late challenge

runners_data.name: Swift Salian
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form, beaten just a head last time and handles this trip well
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who has a progressive profile and went close at Pontefract on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row last May/June (8.3f/1m1f, good/soft) and beaten just a head on this month's reappearance at Pontefract (1m, good to soft); this front-runner has a progressive profile and is one to consider today.

runners_data.name: Harry The Rogue
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who found form over this trip last spring on similar ground
runners_data.comment: Just 2-33 but admirably consistent and went close on last month's stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Just two wins from his 33 starts (both over 1m last spring on good/yielding) but he was highly consistent last year and ran another big race when going close on last month's stable debut at Newcastle (1m, AW); every chance he'll be bang there once more.

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner but hanging right has cost her recently, needs to travel straight
runners_data.comment: 0-7 on turf but this front-runner has been in good form on AW & has shown promise on grass
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 on turf and hanging right on AW has been costly on her last two starts, being demoted from first at Wolverhampton (8.6f) then finishing third at Newcastle (1m; raced mostly alone); however, this front-runner arrives in good heart and has shown promise on grass; could be in the shake-up.

runners_data.name: Two B Tanned
runners_data.note: Course winner returning after 200-day break, front-running style suits if retaining fitness
runners_data.comment: Five wins last April-July and current mark not necessarily beyond her; reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won five times last April-July (good/good to firm), including over C&D; down the field at Nottingham last October when last seen but this mark isn't necessarily beyond her in view of her good third at Haydock (1m, good) in September; could make a bold bid if fully tuned up.

runners_data.name: Ayr Poet
runners_data.note: 11-year-old course winner returning from long break but was in excellent form last season
runners_data.comment: 11yo who won three times last season but there's a suspicion he'll improve for this run
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who was as good as ever last season, winning three times, including at Ayr in September when last season; this two-time course winner is not ruled out on his return but there's a suspicion he'll improve for the run.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with inconsistent profile, needs everything to fall right from the back
runners_data.comment: Won last August but has to be at the very top of his game to win this on his reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Last season's high points were his second at Doncaster (1m, good) in May and a win at Ayr (7f, good) in August; however, he's inconsistent and has to be at the very top of his game to win this on his reappearance.

runners_data.name: Flying Fletcher
runners_data.note: Proven on all-weather but struggling on turf, hold-up style needs strong pace
runners_data.comment: In good form on Newcastle AW this year but not at same level back on turf here recently
runners_data.spotlight: In good form on the Newcastle AW this year but not at the same level back on turf here (1m1f, good) a fortnight ago and now 0-11 on grass.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good form, recent runner-up here over longer trip suggests fitness
runners_data.comment: Six wins last July-October and reappeared with fine second here; leading claims
runners_data.spotlight: Six wins last July-October (various ground) and campaign concluded with a near-miss over C&D; continued the good work when runner-up in a recent 0-95 here (1m1f, good) and he has leading claims back down in grade.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Winless hold-up horse who hasn't been running badly in defeat recently
runners_data.comment: 0-10 but not running badly for this yard and it's possible the return to 1m will suit
runners_data.spotlight: 0-10 and has come seventh on his three starts for this yard (7f/6f); however, he hasn't been running badly, with his latest effort coming in a big field at Thirsk, and there have been hints that his return to 1m may suit.

runners_data.name: Detective
runners_data.note: 10-year-old returning from 208-day layoff, needs the run but was good fresh last April
runners_data.comment: 10yo who returns from some time off but was third over C&D on his reappearance last April
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who has an up-and-down profile last year and this is his first run since September; however, he was a good third over C&D (good) on his reappearance last April and won here (1m1f, good) in July; not ruled out each-way.

runners_data.name: Tilani
runners_data.note: Disappointing since stable switch, needs to prove he retains ability after poor recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Reappearance run gives him something to build on and he's racing off his last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Below par last October on last two runs for Dermot Weld and failed to threaten on recent stable/seasonal debut at Wolverhampton, but that run gives him something to build on and he's racing off his last winning mark today.

races.paceDynamic: Two B Tanned and Eazy On The Eye will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with Swift Salian likely to press them in the early stages. The pace should be honest rather than frantic over this mile trip, creating a searching test that will find out the stamina reserves. With multiple hold-up horses including Barley, Madame De Sevigne, Native Honey, Flying Fletcher, Ashen and Detective all needing to be produced late, the strong early pace will set up perfectly for closers who can handle the decent gallop and have a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned and Eazy On The Eye duel early and maintain honest fractions
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will play into the hands of hold-up horses who can produce late runs. Barley and Madame De Sevigne are perfectly suited to this tactical setup with their proven closing style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners settle into a steadier rhythm without early pressure
scenarios.body: Swift Salian and Harry The Rogue can track the pace and have enough left to outkick the field in the final furlong. Their prominent racing style thrives when not facing a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned gets an uncontested lead with Eazy On The Eye settling behind
scenarios.body: Two B Tanned can dictate terms and kick clear when it matters, using his course winning experience. Eazy On The Eye benefits from the tow and strong pace judgement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint
scenarios.body: Horses with natural speed like Dwindling Funds can benefit from a falsely-run race. The tactical battle becomes about positioning rather than stamina.

watchPoints.text: Two B Tanned faces major fitness test on 200-day return and may not handle the pressure if pressed early
Eazy On The Eye's tendency to hang right could prove costly again if she reverts to old habits under pressure
Barley needed his reappearance run badly so improvement expected with that fitness foundation
Multiple Jim Goldie runners including Ayr Poet, Native Honey, Dwindling Funds and Ashen create tactical complications
Several apprentice jockeys carry valuable weight allowances but lack tactical experience in competitive handicap

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Bright is the lone confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the gates, likely setting a steady gallop without pressure. Donna Nook, Polygram, Glorious Kitty, and Salaria can track prominently but none are confirmed pace pressers. With eight hold-up horses including Epidavros, Naturalia, and Bearin Up, this creates a tactical affair where the lone leader gets an easy time of it. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace, as the large hold-up contingent will struggle to make up ground from too far back over 1m1f.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sovereign Bright Leads All
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Bright gets uncontested fractions and stays the extended trip.
scenarios.body: The 3yo mare gets first run on the field and her class edge shows when others struggle to reel her in from distance. Her turf form reads better than her AW efforts and she's unexposed at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers can slip the leader turning for home.
scenarios.body: Glorious Kitty or Donna Nook track the pace perfectly and have enough tactical speed to collar Sovereign Bright in the final furlong. The hold-up horses are caught too far back to respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Epidavros or Naturalia benefit from a slowly-run race that becomes a dash, using their finishing kick to maximum effect. The front runners tie up having gone too slow early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge Sovereign Bright early creating fast fractions.
scenarios.body: The early pace becomes unsustainable and the entire field comes back to the closers in the final quarter-mile. A rank outsider from the back picks up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Sovereign Bright must be respected as the lone pace setter getting an uncontested lead
Watch if any of the prominent horses decide to pressure Sovereign Bright early which could change the complexion
Storm On Jura returning after 195 days off with a tendency to fade could struggle badly
Several 5lb claimers riding including inexperienced apprentices who may get outpaced tactically
Glorious Kitty finished close second at Beverley and represents the main threat to track the leader

runners_data.spotlight: Close third at Beverley (8.5f) 11 days ago and she's won twice there at 1m2f, but her record at 1m3f-1m4f (six races) is less convincing.

runners_data.name: Furhaan

runners_data.spotlight: Won handicap debut at Windsor (11.5f, heavy) in September and creditable fifth at Yarmouth (11.5f, good) the following month; left Ed Walker for 32,000gns in October and last week's reappearance (25-1) did not suggest an imminent return to winning form.

races.paceDynamic: Night Breeze will likely set the early tempo from the prominent position, with Hamlet's Night, Eroico and Rising Sky tracking close behind in the opening stages. The pace should be genuine but sustainable given the 1m4½f distance, with no confirmed tearaway leaders to create early pressure. This sets up a race where the hold-up horses like Fast Fred, Princess Niyla, Letsbefrank and Furhaan can settle off the pace and deliver late challenges. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can benefit from the galloping finish that this moderate early pace will create.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Night Breeze sets a steady tempo without early pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows closers to settle perfectly and unleash powerful finishing kicks in the straight. Fast Fred and Furhaan are ideally positioned to exploit this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens beyond sustainable levels
scenarios.body: Night Breeze and Hamlet's Night gain crucial positioning advantages while the hold-up brigade faces too much to do. Their tactical positioning becomes the decisive factor in a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If Night Breeze goes too slowly and creates a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test over the final 3f where natural pace horses hold sway. Rising Sky and Princess Niyla benefit from their handier positions in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Even gallop throughout
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners engage Night Breeze early
scenarios.body: The sustained pace plays to horses with proven stamina at this trip. Letsbefrank's staying power and Fast Fred's recent course form become crucial assets.

watchPoints.text: Night Breeze could set an unsustainably slow pace if allowed an easy lead, turning this into a sprint
Hamlet's Night's 0-13 turf record is alarming despite his recent hurdles form suggesting ability
Fast Fred's 4lb rise may not stop him given his excellent recent course form and ideal running style
Rising Sky's tongue-tie debut on turf could significantly alter her race-running approach
Furhaan's yard switch to Jim Goldie could unlock improvement given trainer's 2/20 recent record

runners_data.name: Backspin
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran well when third at Doncaster on good ground four weeks ago on seasonal reappearance
runners_data.comment: Third of 16 at Doncaster on stable/seasonal debut and he's one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned mostly on AW for Richard Hughes, for whom he won at Southwell last March, but he ran well when third of 16 at Doncaster (7f, good to soft) four weeks ago on his stable/seasonal debut; he's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose mark continues to slide and ran fairly at Thirsk just eight days ago on quick turnaround
runners_data.comment: Ran fairly well on second start for Jim Goldie but needs another step in right direction
runners_data.spotlight: Her mark continues to slide and she ran fairly well at Thirsk (7f, good) last week on her second start for Jim Goldie, who should get a win out of her at some point; however, she needs another step in the right direction today.

races.paceDynamic: Master Richard and Royalty Bay will set the early tempo as both confirmed front runners clash from the off. With Benacre, Mister Bluebird, Aisling Oscar and Salam Dubawi also keen to race prominently, the pace will be honest through the first half-mile. This sustained gallop will stretch the field and create opportunities for the strong-finishing hold-up horses to pick off tired leaders in the final furlong. The race shape clearly favours hold-up performers who can deliver late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Master Richard and Royalty Bay engage early with prominent racers pressuring throughout
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will find out the pace-setters in the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses with finishing kicks to sweep past tired leaders. Late runners with stamina reserves will prosper most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners settle more than expected and the pace becomes moderate
scenarios.body: Prominent racers can track the steadier gallop and kick clear before the hold-up horses can mount their challenges. Those positioned just off the pace will have first run on the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: End-to-End Gallop Favours Stamina
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes extremely strong with multiple pace-setters going too fast too soon
scenarios.body: The searching gallop will collapse the entire field in the final two furlongs, favouring only those with proven stamina reserves. Pure staying power trumps tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Master Richard or Royalty Bay establishes a clear early lead without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The pace-setter can dictate fractions and kick clear when the field comes to challenge. Front running tactics succeed when not subjected to sustained pressure.

races.name: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Whimsy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needs the pace to be strong to be effective, 17 days since last run gives him a freshness edge
runners_data.comment: Very solid Flat record for this trainer suggests she will be on the premises
runners_data.spotlight: Had three seasons with Andrew Balding, including three wins, and has been with this yard since July 2023, including for two wins (one over hurdles) and plenty of place returns; third over 1m4f in her only two Flat runs in the last 13 months, including under Patrick McGettigan 17 days ago, and her very solid Flat record for this trainer suggests she will be on the premises.

runners_data.name: St Faz
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with recent AW form for new stable, 23-day break since last start could have him spot-on
runners_data.comment: 3-3 on AW last month upon joining this yard, before he was hampered at the start last time
runners_data.spotlight: Seen mostly over jumps in his Irish days; 3-3 on AW (1m6f/2m) last month upon joining this stable, before a lesser show three weeks ago when getting hampered at the start prevented his usual tactics; not ruled out on return to turf.

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 246-day absence is a major concern despite previous course success
runners_data.comment: Last in Melrose at York (14-1 in hat-trick bid) last August; could be of renewed interest
runners_data.spotlight: Won small-field races at Hamilton for a maiden (1m3f, good to firm) last May and handicap (1m5f, good) last July; seriously raised in class when tailed-off last at 14-1 in the Melrose Handicap at York (1m6f, good to firm; again sweating) last August, but he could be of renewed interest on this reappearance for an in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong course record including three C&D wins, 4lb higher than last Musselburgh success
runners_data.comment: Plentiful form here; promise on reappearance (50-1); could be a lot more potent this time
runners_data.spotlight: Plentiful form at Musselburgh with three C&D wins, including last August for his only Flat win last year (4lb higher today); never dangerous when 50-1 for reappearance here two weeks ago but showed promise from out the back and could be a lot more potent this time.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 582-day layoff, massive question mark over fitness despite dropping only 3lb
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in September 2024 on sole run for this yard; dropped just 3lb in his absence
runners_data.spotlight: 4-15 for David Simcock, including two wins in summer 2024, before tailed off that September on his only appearance for this yard; dropped just 3lb in his absence and probably best watched this time.

runners_data.name: Senor Cortez
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who will dictate the pace, encouraging debut run for new trainer five weeks ago
runners_data.comment: Scored twice last August and made an encouraging start for his new yard five weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Scored twice (1m6f/2m) for Darryll Holland last August and made an encouraging start for his new yard when third to St Faz on Lingfield AW five weeks ago; the first of those wins was impressive over 1m6f on good to firm and he's one to consider despite today's 15lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Alther Walden
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form, will need pace to develop to show his finishing kick

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong Musselburgh record but concerning recent form trend, apprentice takes 5lb off
runners_data.comment: 4-11 at Musselburgh; soundly beaten at 40-1 here on reappearance three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: 4-11 at Musselburgh, including three 1m6f/2m wins on good ground last May-October; also scored at Nottingham in October, a runaway win over 2m2f on heavy going which sees him 3lb higher today; soundly beaten at 40-1 here on reappearance three weeks ago and, judged on last season, it may take him another run before he refinds his form.

races.paceDynamic: Senor Cortez will lead from the gates with no other confirmed pace-setters in this field, allowing him to dictate a comfortable rhythm through the early stages. St Faz and Talismans Time will likely track prominently behind the leader, but neither has the natural speed to apply serious pressure. The lack of pace competition means the gallop will be steady rather than searching, with the hold-up horses like Simple Star, Mountain Road, Alther Walden and Whimsy having plenty of ground to make up in the straight. This shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and get first run on the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Cortez maintains his rhythm without serious challenge through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The leader gets an easy time of it and has enough left to repel late challengers, with the prominent runners best placed to capitalize if he falters. The hold-up horses face too much ground to make up against the controlled pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If St Faz or Talismans Time apply subtle pressure to soften up the leader
scenarios.body: The more experienced campaigners among the prominent group use their tactical positioning to strike at the right moment when the leader begins to tire. Simple Star's course knowledge becomes crucial from his hold-up position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and the field bunches up significantly
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the back-markers to stay in touch and unleash finishing kicks, with Mountain Road's class advantage and Alther Walden's recent form telling late. The prominent horses get swamped by superior finishing speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses decide to make moves simultaneously from halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint from a long way out, suiting whoever has the most natural speed and tactical speed rather than stamina. Trojan Sun's recent poor form continues as the race doesn't develop to suit anyone's natural style.

runners_data.name: Archduke Ferdinand

runners_data.comment: He's 3lb below his last winning mark but he needs to get back on track
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner who has dropped to a mark 3lb lower than when winning at Redcar (6f, good to firm) last May; he could improve for this month's reappearance run over C&D but he failed to threaten, which was also the case on his final few outings last season; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Pop Star

runners_data.comment: On a reduced mark but he's struggled to get competitive on his six runs since December

runners_data.name: Albegone

runners_data.name: Arnhem

runners_data.spotlight: He did well after joining this yard last year and he's on a handy mark; he should get back on track sooner or later but this 10yo has failed to shine on his last three outings, over C&D on last two starts.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle

races.paceDynamic: Ziggy's Triton will lead from the gates with Mon Na Slieve, Archduke Ferdinand, South Parade, Pop Star and I'm Next providing prominent company in this competitive sprint. The early pace will be solid but sustainable given the number of prominent runners sharing the workload, with no obvious speed merchants to inject severe pressure. The hold-up horses - Jer Batt, Reigning Profit, Albegone, Arnhem, Knicks, Montezuma and Azuinthejungle - face a tactical disadvantage as the even pace will leave them with ground to make up in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours prominent/pressing horses who can track the pace and kick from ideal positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady without collapsing, allowing trackers to strike.
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get first run on the field while hold-up horses struggle to close from too far back. Mon Na Slieve, I'm Next and Ziggy's Triton benefit most from their forward positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes too fast early due to competitive positioning.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens beyond sustainable levels, setting up the race for the hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders. Montezuma and Albegone capitalize on their patient tactics while the early leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ziggy's Triton Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Triton gets an uncontested lead and controls fractions.
scenarios.body: The front-runner dictates comfortable splits and has enough left to resist late challenges. His course and distance win last August and recent form turnaround make this viable despite limited early pace pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the solid early pace becomes a crawl in the middle stages.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the three-furlong pole, suiting horses with natural speed regardless of position. This tactical lottery could favor any runner with a strong turn of foot over those relying on tactical positioning.
